description: manifest.json at the root of an activation-capture directory, beside examples.jsonl and shard_NNNNN.npz

notes.capture_backend: Emitted by the Rust writer only. The Python writer predates it and no reader requires it, so it is writer-only rather than required. Adding it to the Python writer is a behavior change that belongs in its own commit.
notes.dataset_sha256: Not comparable across writers. Rust hashes the file's raw bytes (std::fs::read); Python hashes text-mode f.read(), which normalizes CRLF to LF. The two digests agree for an LF-only dataset and differ for a CRLF one. Both are internally consistent; neither is wrong. Do not 'fix' one side to match the other without deciding which domain the field means and bumping schema_version - a test pins the divergence so a one-sided change fails.
notes.tokenizer_fingerprint: Not comparable across writers, and documented as such at activation-capture.rs:287-291. Python hashes name_or_path, len(tokenizer), and the chat template; Rust hashes the model file path, the vocabulary length, and an empty template, because a raw-text capture applies no template. Each keeps its own artifacts internally consistent from capture through train to score.
notes.envelope: The required set is a superset of the shared report envelope in common/reports.py: schema_version, exactly one discriminator (artifact), a stamp (created), and git_sha. Both writers satisfy validate_report today, though that module scopes itself to reports rather than artifact manifests.
